wording.title: The poles no longer collapse the stable step
wording.x_axis: Torus width M (computed points = M squared)

source_origin: figure-pack/ is written by scripts/prepare_figures.py from the saved measurements in data/ (checked against data/manifest.json); no earlier plot was read
uncertainty: none shown and none exists: values are deterministic measured errors or model outputs, not replicate estimates
r_definition: r is the largest stable step from the TC5 bisection divided by the equatorial wave-crossing time.
r_denominator: Equatorial spacing is from a lat-lon grid with the same computed-point count; wave speed is the initial maximum sqrt(gD) + |v|. Bisection tolerance is 2%.
transformations: r is plotted unchanged; value labels are r rounded to two decimals
x is log2 with ticks at the three tested widths; y is linear from 0 to 3
the connecting line only joins the three measured widths in order; it is not a fit or an interpolation claim

encoding.torus: blue filled circles joined by a blue line

status: deterministic stability bisection results; one value per width, no replicates, no interval
alt_text: Line and point plot of the largest stable step divided by the equatorial wave-crossing time for torus widths M of 64, 128 and 256 in the TC5 case over 50 simulated days. The ratio is 2.45, 2.32 and 2.25: it stays bounded near 2.3 instead of collapsing as the grid refines, though it is not constant.

render.svg: 622.5 pt wide, which is 830 CSS px; text converted to paths so it renders identically without DejaVu Sans installed; a colour-bar gradient, where present, is embedded as a raster at 4x CSS density
render.png: 1660 x 1294 px, RGB, no alpha, for display at 830 CSS px
